Incumbent [[Angus King]] was re-elected to a second term in office in a landslide against [[James B. Longley Jr.]], [[Thomas J. Connolly]], and [[Pat LaMarche]]. This election was the first since [[1982 Maine gubernatorial election|1982]] in which the winning candidate received greater than 50 percent of the popular vote and the last such election until [[2018 Maine gubernatorial election|2018]]. As of 2026, this is the most recent election in which Maine elected an independent governor and in which any candidate won every county in the state. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== *[[Thomas J. Longley did carry 22 municipalities in rural northern and eastern Maine and tied King in two other municipalities. Connolly won only the [[Passamaquoddy Indian Township Reservation]], though he did tie King in the small town of [[Beddington, Maine|Beddington]] (at four votes apiece). Clarke carried the town of [[Talmadge, Maine|Talmadge]], eight votes to seven for King.
